title: EEG and clinical predictors of medically intractable childhood epilepsy

title: Response to first drug trial predicts outcome in childhood temporal lobe epilepsy

While they attempted to capture a mix of severity via satellite centers, the reliance on tertiary/specialty referral patterns introduces a moderate risk of selection bias.
D1_Source_Evidence: Patients with TLE between 1 and 18 years old seen in the Division of Neurology at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia during 1999 were identified through billing records and chart review.
D1_Source_Reasoning: The target population (children with TLE in a specific geographic/clinical catchment) is clearly defined.
D1_Method_Evidence: Potential patients were identified through centralized billing records, using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Edition (ICD-9) codes... D1_Method_Reasoning: The identification method is clear, but the authors explicitly state it is not population-based, which may exclude patients managed in primary care.
D1_Period_Evidence: seen for an outpatient visit in the Division of Neurology at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) during 1999 with onset of epilepsy after 1996.
D1_Period_Reasoning: The specific year of recruitment and the window for epilepsy onset are provided.

D1_Place_Reasoning: The geographic and clinical settings are well-described.
